title: Implementing monthly interdisciplinary deprescribing rounds across three long-term care homes
subtitle: Implementation study organised by RE-AIM, using routine records
statement: Residents of three long-term care homes (168 beds) take a median of nine regular medicines, and review repeatedly finds sedatives, proton pump inhibitors and preventive medicines that no longer serve them. Monthly interdisciplinary deprescribing rounds were welcomed in one home but stopped whenever the pharmacist was absent. The operator wants rounds in all three homes; the open questions are whether they can be adopted and sustained, how many residents they reach, and whether their recommendations are carried out.
whoAffected: Frail older residents, many near the end of life, their families and substitute decision-makers, and the nurses, physicians and pharmacist who run the rounds.
whatHurts: Medicines that no longer help add falls, confusion, swallowing burden and administration time; reviews that happen only when one person is present leave most residents unreviewed.
currentPractice: Ad hoc medication review at admission and when problems arise; one home held monthly rounds last year until the pharmacist's leave interrupted them.
whyNow: The operator has approved rounds and pharmacist time for 2027, and the one-home experience showed that sustainability, not enthusiasm, is the problem to solve.
constraints: No research funding. The consultant pharmacist has 0.4 FTE across the three homes. Data must come from existing medication administration records, round notes and incident reports, with no new forms for care staff. Every recommendation must respect the wishes of the resident or substitute decision-maker.
patientCenteredGoal: Each resident takes only the medicines that still serve their goals, decided with them or their family, and changes are carried out and followed up.
summary: Problem framed as an implementation question: adoption, reach, fidelity and sustainability of deprescribing rounds.
